A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HOH benchmark study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, Appendices A–E, and supplementary prompts support reliable comparison. The additional page in v3 results from the expanded bibliography.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval and generation experiments in Section 5, plus factual-change classification, human validation, and supplementary model evaluations in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the appendix comparisons of temporal retrieval methods, GPT-4o experiments, and long-answer evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same factual-change extraction, classifier, QA generation and update procedures, and temporally weighted search engine. No method component or objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same June–November 2024 Wikipedia snapshots, HOH dataset and retrieval corpus, and factual-change, retrieval, short-answer, and long-answer evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: The comparison methods and evaluated models are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. MRAG and TempRALM already participate in v2 Table 15; v3 supplies their citations without adding comparators.

E3.justification: The 10,000-question evaluation set, 1,000-sample GPT-4o subset, classifier split, retrieval settings, generation controls, and evaluation metrics are unchanged (Section 4; Appendices B, D, and E).

E4.justification: Both retain the same input-representation ablations, passage-number and ordering experiments, timeliness-awareness analysis, and manual validation. No supplementary analysis or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report the same point estimates and validation statistics. Neither reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and reported findings are unchanged across the main text and appendices. This includes Figures 3–4, the temporal-retrieval comparison in Table 15, GPT-4o results in Tables 16–17, and long-answer results in Tables 19–20.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 retains the same processing-time decomposition and efficiency reasoning, and Appendix D.2 retains the same hit-rate formulation. No definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark novelty and construction claims, and the same claims that outdated information reduces RAG accuracy and increases harmful responses.

C2.justification: Interpretations of retrieval tradeoffs, passage ordering, and timeliness awareness are unchanged. Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning update frequency, single-article questions, and homogeneous historical documents.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and software specifications, data fields, prompts, and the code/data access statement are unchanged (Appendices B–D; Tables 21–22; Figures 5–13).

R1.justification: v3 resolves missing citations and adds five bibliography entries: Yu et al. (2024), Cheng et al. (2025), and Ouyang et al. (2024) in the introduction, plus Siyue et al. (2025) and Gade and Jetcheva (2024) for MRAG and TempRALM in Appendix E.2. This completes attribution without substantively changing research positioning.

P1.justification: Textual corrections replace question-mark citation placeholders with author–year citations and update the arXiv version/date text. Scientific prose, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Longer citations cause local text reflow on pages 1–5 and in Appendix E.2, and the bibliography expands from two pages to three. Figures, table designs, captions, and their contents remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 contains unresolved citations in the introduction and for the temporal retrieval baselines in Appendix E.2. v3 supplies identifiable citations and full references, modestly improving attribution and traceability. The scientific evidence, analyses, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
